finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::write-capable undo()/redo() have no read-only/permission gate; the read-only check lives only in the two view-level callers
evidence: The mechanical observation is right: `YorkieNoteStore.undo()`/`redo()` (yorkie-note-store.ts, the `undo()`/`redo()` methods) take no readOnly/permission argument, and `NoteEditorAPI.undo()` in editor.ts calls `runHistory('undo')` unconditionally — the store simply has no notion of readOnly. But the described defect (a viewer-role session writing reverse ops into the shared doc) cannot occur as the code stands. `undo()` first checks `canUndo()`, which requires `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`, and `undoFloor` is captured at construction; a read-only mount never produces a local document change (notes-view.tsx skips `ensureText` when readOnly, `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` is set outside any compartment so a vim keymap switch cannot flip it, and note-sync only forwards non-remote user-event transactions), so the local undo/redo stacks stay empty and both calls return early without touching the CRDT. Combined with the reviewer's own admission that no reachable caller exists, this is a defense-in-depth/layering observation rather than a present defect; the claim's specific attack chain (including "a keymap switch whose editable facet changes") misreads the wiring.
